title: Replying to @Craig Caruso #broadway #musicaltheatre #spiderman #theat...
transcript: if there is one misconception about the Spider Man musical that I wanna clear up for everyone it's that contrary to popular belief not a single person died welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history so this myth that people died during Spider Man Turn Off the dark is extremely pervasive I hear it from theatre people and non-theatre people alike but it is simply not true what did happen is that there were a number of injuries some of them quite serious and people started making jokes like “oh, people are dying left and right” “they won't have any actors left alive soon” and that spun out of control to the point where to this day I still get people asking me earnestly “how many people died during Spider Man again?” but no one did I'm gonna talk more about the injuries in a second but let's rewind a bit so for personal context I saw the show back in 2011 I actually got to go backstage afterwards, which was fun but I was at the 100th preview which is hilarious famously, the show had a record-breaking 182 preview performances over the course of almost six months before they were able to officially open somewhere in the middle of that they also took a hiatus of a couple weeks to make massive changes to the book they fired Julie Taymor and eventually they opened in June 2011 people began referring to it as Spider Man 1.0 versus 2.0 but I saw the 1.0 version which had the infamous shoe number as well as the crew of three nerdy narrators called the Geek chorus I look back on this show with a lot of complicated feelings because at the time I was very much a defender of it like I won't necessarily defend the book but the score definitely had some bangers but more importantly of course, in this case, I found the spectacle to be pretty extraordinary and I've always felt that one of the things that separates regular spectacle from Julie Taymor spectacle is that it's not just cool it's also smart I often think about this moment toward the beginning of the show where they're live-weaving this giant tapestry on stage by having the aerialists swing back and forth and the strips of cloth going up in between each swing like this is one of the coolest things in the show and it's not even that high tech it's just clever and don't get me wrong the high tech stuff was also, frankly, pretty cool I think where my opinion has changed the most over the years is that back then, I was a teenager and I was going around saying things like “hey everybody, lay off the Spider Man musical” “okay, injuries happen in Broadway shows all the time” “and the only reason it's getting so much publicity right now” “is because everyone's out to get the show” “it's just an easy target that we're all dog piling on” and there's not zero truth to that I definitely think people were having fun at the show's expense but as I've gotten older, I've come to recognize that the frequency and intensity of injuries could only really have been caused by an irresponsibly unsafe work environment and that ultimately human safety is far more important than artistic ambition but if we are just assessing the show artistically I still will kind of defend it in certain ways despite the show's many flaws I've always said that it's a great example of adapting the source material to fit the new medium I've always believed that any source material *could* make a good musical if you just conceive it and approach it the right way (and then follow through on that with good execution) and I will die on the hill that this was the correct approach to take for a Spider Man musical: big spectacle, rock score, allowing it to be kind of campy and taking a visual approach that honored the comic book origin While also allowing this auteur director to infuse it with her bizarre, aesthetic sensibility because yeah, this show was weird in a way that very few IP musicals are allowed to be very few musicals in general frankly and again I'll admit the execution of this approach was questionable but conceptually? I gotta say, no notes
